entry.name: sfrecord~
entry.digest: Record to audio file on disk
entry.description: Use the sfrecord~ object to record and save MSP output as an audio file.

arguments.name: number-of-input-channels
arguments.description: Sets the number of input channels, which determines the number of inlets that theobject will have. The maximum number of channels is 64, and the default is 1. The audio file created will have the same number of channels as this argument. Whether you can actually record the maximum number of channels is dependent on the speed of your processor and hard disk.

arguments.name: buffer-size
arguments.description: An optional second argument sets the buffer size. The defult value is 20160.

messages.name: int
messages.description: In left inlet: If a file has been opened with themessage, a non-zero value begins recording, andstops recording and closes the file.requires anothermessage to record again if ahas been sent.Recording may also stop spontaneously if there is an error, such as running out of space on your hard disk.

messages.name: loop
messages.description: In left inlet: If a file has been opened with themessage, the word, followed by a length in milliseconds, begins a recording that captures the most recent audio in the specified amount of time. The recording will stop when theobject receives 0 in its left inlet.

messages.name: open
messages.description: In left inlet: Opens a file for recording. By default, the file type is AIFF, butalso supports WAVE, OGG, FLAC, and Raw Data. The word, without an argument, brings up a standard Save As dialog allowing you to choose a filename. The optional symbols,,,, orspecify the file format (which can also be set in the Save As dialog with a Format pop-up menu). Ifis followed by a second symbol, it creates a file in the current default volume. An existing file with the same name will be overwritten. The format symbol (e.g.,) can follow the optional filename argument. If only one argument is given to themessage, which is a filename, the file type is determined from the file extension (e.g., "open test.wav" sets the file type to).

messages.name: print
messages.digest: Output status information about recording progress
messages.description: Outputs cryptic status information about the progress of the recording.

messages.name: record
messages.digest: Record for a specified amount of time
messages.description: In left inlet: If a file has been opened with themessage, the word, followed by a time in milliseconds, begins recording for the specified amount of time. The recording can be stopped before it reaches the end by sendingato its left inlet.

messages.name: samptype
messages.digest: Specify the sample type to use when recording
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a symbol, specifies the sample type to use when recording the audio file. The following types of sample data are supported:: 8-bit integer: 16-bit integer: 24-bit integer: 32-bit integer: 32-bit floating-point: 64-bit floating-point: 8-bit "mu"-law encoding: 8-bit a-law encodingThe optional second argument, a 0 or 1, specifies whether or not byte-swapping should be used, which is only useful when writing a 'raw' audio file.

messages.name: signal
messages.description: Each inlet ofaccepts a signal which is recorded to a channel of an audio file when recording is turned on.
